cards.front: Recall a key point about Film and Computer Gaming Music 1990s-Present
cards.back: Film music uses leitmotifs (recurring themes for characters/ideas) — Williams' Star Wars themes are textbook examples of orchestral leitmotif technique.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Film and Computer Gaming Music 1990s-Present
cards.back: Underscoring supports the on-screen action without dominating; hit points sync musical events with dramatic moments on screen.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Film and Computer Gaming Music 1990s-Present
cards.back: Gaming music must be INTERACTIVE — it adapts to player actions through horizontal resequencing or vertical layering, unlike linear film scores.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Film and Computer Gaming Music 1990s-Present
cards.back: Modern film/gaming scores blend orchestral instruments with synthesisers, sampled sounds and electronic production — hybrid scoring is now the norm.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Identify leitmotif technique by name. Explain the difference between linear (film) and interactive (game) scoring. Analyse hybrid orchestration. Use film/gaming vocabulary (underscoring, hit point, source music).

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Film and game music is just background music — it does not need serious analysis. Correct: Film and game music uses sophisticated compositional techniques: leitmotif, thematic transformation, underscoring, hit points, and interactive adaptive systems.
